REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
CLO INDENTURE — TRIDENT COUNTERPARTY MARKUP
Structured Finance / Securitization Practice

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
Prepared for: Deal Team
Re: Analysis of Trident counterparty markup against the base form indenture

----------------------------------------------------------------------
I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

This memorandum provides a comprehensive redline review of the Trident counterparty markup of the base form CLO indenture. It reconciles every deviation introduced in the counterparty's redline against the base materials, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the deal team's controlling client instructions. It is intended to equip the deal team with a complete, prioritized view of the counterparty markup and a recommended negotiating posture on each deviation.

The review is grounded in the following operative materials:
  • Base form indenture (underlying the matter; "Deal materials" file)
  • Trident counterparty markup (the "Trident redline")
  • Disclosure schedules and exhibits (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, Exhibit B survival matrix)
  • Deal team/client email correspondence (controlling instruction in the latest message)
  • Engagement cover letter, firm playbook, and offering memorandum ("OM") excerpt as referenced in the engagement instruction

Consistent with the engagement instruction, we also reviewed the cover letter, the firm playbook on structured-finance indenture negotiation, and the relevant OM excerpt as contextual reference materials. Those were considered alongside the base form indenture in assessing whether each Trident revision reflects acceptable market practice or a departure requiring rejection or counter.

The Trident redline accepts most firm-standard provisions in the base indenture. However, it introduces three material deviations that must be considered in sequence:

  (1) a silent reduction of the indemnification cap coupled with a conversion of the indemnity basket from a deductible to a "tipping" basket;
  (2) an expansion of the Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") definition to carve out regulatory action of precisely the kind at issue in this matter; and
  (3) a new shortened limitation period that reduces the survival period for the core representations.

Each deviation is analyzed below, reconciled against the base materials, the disclosure schedules, Exhibit B, and the controlling client instruction.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
II. CONTROLLING CLIENT INSTRUCTIONS — DEAL TEAM CORRESPONDENCE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The deal correspondence contains a partner email thread whose messages state conflicting analysis priorities. The latest message in the thread REVERSES the priorities set out in the earlier messages and represents the controlling instruction. We have applied the latest message as the operative mandate for this memorandum:

  • The client will concede the conversion of the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
  • The client treats any reduction to the survival period for the core representations as a walk-away issue (i.e., non-negotiable).
  • The earlier messages' contrary priority ordering is superseded and is not applied.

This instruction materially shapes the recommended posture on Deviations 1 and 3 below. Deviation 1 (basket conversion) is conceded by the client and should not be negotiated back; however, the companion cap reduction within the same deviation must still be addressed because the client's concession covers only the basket conversion, not a further cap reduction. Deviation 3 (survival-period reduction) is a walk-away item and must be rejected in full.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION: SILENT CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------

A. What the Trident redline changes

The Trident markup revises the indemnification provision in two ways:

  (i) It silently reduces the aggregate indemnification cap from the firm-standard amount in the base indenture.
  (ii) It converts the indemnity basket from a deductible (under which the indemnitor is liable only for losses in excess of the basket amount, dollar-for-dollar above it) to a "tipping" basket (under which, once the specified threshold is exceeded, the indemnitor becomes liable for the full amount, including the amounts below the basket).

B. Reconciliation against the base materials and Schedule 5.2

The base form indenture establishes a firm-standard indemnification cap and a deductible-type basket. The Trident reduction of the cap narrows the availability of indemnity protection and shifts cost/risk allocation against the insured/buyer side of the deal.

Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that remain with the relevant party under the base indenture. The Trident markup's indemnification changes would silently shift a portion of those retained liabilities onto the other party, because the reduced cap plus the tipping-basket mechanics alter (i) when indemnity becomes payable and (ii) the aggregate amount payable. Any revision that would transfer Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities must be identified and, absent explicit agreement, resisted. Schedule 5.2 controls over the general statements in the base materials, so the deliverable must reconcile the indemnification markup against those scheduled retained liabilities.

C. Client instruction and recommended posture

Under the controlling client instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping). Accordingly:

  • Basket conversion: CONCEDE. The tipping-basket mechanism is not to be negotiated back. This reflects the client's explicit instruction.
  • Silent cap reduction: NOT COVERED by the client's concession and must be addressed. The cap reduction is a separate and material erosion of the indemnity protection. We recommend rejecting the cap reduction absent compelling market justification, or, at a minimum, requiring a counter that restores the cap to the firm-standard level. Because Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities control, we should not permit the cap reduction to operate as an indirect reassignment of those retained liabilities.

D. Negotiating points

  1. Reject the silent reduction in the indemnification cap; propose reinstating the base indenture cap.
  2. Accept the tipping-basket conversion per client instruction, but confirm in drafting that the tipping threshold and mechanics produce no further adverse shift beyond the conceded conversion.
  3. Obtain confirmation from Trident that the indemnity changes do not reallocate any Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; if they do, require carve-out language preserving the scheduled allocation.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. DEVIATION 2 — MAE DEFINITION: REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

A. What the Trident redline changes

The Trident markup expands the definition of Material Adverse Effect by adding carve-outs for "regulatory action" of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. In effect, this would exclude certain regulatory events or inquiries from what constitutes a material adverse effect, narrowing the circumstances in which a party could invoke an MAE-based remedy or condition.

B. Reconciliation against the base materials and Schedule 3.7

The base form indenture's MAE definition does not include these regulatory-action carve-outs; their addition is a new departure from the firm-standard base.

Schedule 3.7 of the disclosure schedules discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. Because the carve-outs are drafted to exclude regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue," they directly intersect with the two pending inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7. This is not a benign drafting refinement: the carve-outs would operate to preclude the client from relying on MAE with respect to events arising out of the very regulatory inquiries already pending and disclosed. Under the base materials, Schedule 3.7's scheduled exceptions control over general statements; therefore, the MAE carve-outs must be analyzed against the specific pending inquiries identified in that schedule.

C. Recommended posture

The MAE carve-outs are a material narrowing of a core protective provision as it bears directly on the two scheduled regulatory inquiries. This is a substantive deviation that materially disadvantages the client in precisely the scenario that matters most in this deal. We recommend:

  1. REJECT the regulatory-action carve-outs as drafted.
  2. At minimum, redraft the carve-outs to exclude only pre-agreed, enumerated regulatory events that are not connected to the Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries, or exempt the two pending inquiries from the carve-out so the client retains an MAE remedy tied to them.
  3. Confirm that no carve-out is broad enough to cover regulatory action arising from or related to the Schedule 3.7 inquiries.

D. Interaction with Exhibit B and survival

Because these MAE carve-outs bear on the client's ability to invoke remedies over the life of the indenture, they interact with the survival period and the survival matrix in Exhibit B (see Deviation 3 below). A shortened survival period would further narrow the window in which the client could assert an MAE-based claim. The two deviations therefore compound one another and should be addressed together.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
V. DEVIATION 3 — LIMITATION PERIOD: SHORTENED SURVIVAL FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

A. What the Trident redline changes

The Trident markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival period for the core representations from the period set in the base indenture and reflected in Exhibit B.

B. Reconciliation against the base materials and Exhibit B

Exhibit B of the disclosure materials sets the survival matrix for the deal, i.e., the operative periods during which each category of representation survives for claims purposes. The Trident limitation-period change directly contradicts Exhibit B's survival matrix by shortening the survival of the core representations.

Under the base materials, the scheduled survival matrix in Exhibit B controls over general statements. The markup's new limitation period therefore creates a direct conflict with the controlling schedule. Because Exhibit B sets the negotiated bargain on survival, any unilateral shortening by Trident must be treated as a deviation from the controlling document.

C. Client instruction and recommended posture — WALK-AWAY ISSUE

The controlling client instruction is unambiguous:

  • "The client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue."

This means the survival-period reduction is non-negotiable from the client's perspective. Accordingly:

  1. REJECT the shortened survival period outright.
  2. Do not offer a counter that reduces survival below the Exhibit B baseline for the core representations.
  3. Treat Trident's insistence on any survival reduction for the core representations as a deal-breaker requiring escalation, consistent with the client's walk-away mandate.

D. Interaction with Deviation 2

As noted above, the shortened survival period would compound the MAE carve-outs by limiting the time in which the client could bring an MAE-based or representation-based claim at all. Even if the MAE carve-outs were resolved favorably, a truncated survival window would independently defeat the remedy. This further supports treating this deviation as a walk-away item.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. SUMMARY OF DEVIATIONS AND RECOMMENDED POSTURE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The table below summarizes each deviation, its source, the controlling reconciliation, and the recommended posture consistent with the latest client instruction.

  Deviation | Trident Change | Base Material / Schedule Conflict | Recommended Posture
  ----------|----------------|-----------------------------------|---------------------
  1a | Indemnification cap silently reduced | Reduces firm-standard cap; risks shifting Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities | REJECT cap reduction; request reinstatement of base cap
  1b | Basket converted from deductible to tipping | Not separately contested per client instruction | CONCEDE per client instruction (basket conversion)
  2 | MAE definition adds regulatory-action carve-outs intersecting Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries | Schedule 3.7 controls; carve-outs would defeat MAE remedy on disclosed inquiries | REJECT/redraft carve-outs to exclude the Schedule 3.7 inquiries
  3 | New limitation period shortens survival of core representations | Contradicts Exhibit B survival matrix | WALK-AWAY ISSUE — REJECT; no survival reduction acceptable

----------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONS AND DRAFTING NOTES
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  • Concession scope: The client's concession is strictly limited to the basket conversion (Deviation 1b). It does not extend to the cap reduction (Deviation 1a), the MAE carve-outs (Deviation 2), or the survival-period change (Deviation 3).
  • Superseded instruction: Earlier messages in the partner thread stated a different priority ordering; those are superseded by the latest message and have no effect on this analysis.
  • Schedules control: Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B control over general statements in the base materials. Any drafting must preserve the allocations and survival matrix those schedules establish.
  • Compounding risk: Deviations 2 and 3 are cumulative; resolving one without the other leaves the client exposed on the same core protections.
  • Misfiled correspondence: The matter folder contains correspondence from an unrelated engagement; such materials have been disregarded and do not inform this analysis.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
VIII. CONCLUSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The Trident counterparty markup accepts most firm-standard provisions in the base CLO indenture but introduces three material deviations. The deal team's controlling instruction concedes the basket conversion (Deviation 1b) but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue (Deviation 3, reject). The indemnification cap reduction (Deviation 1a) and the MAE regulatory carve-outs (Deviation 2) must each be rejected or redrafted, with particular attention to the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation and the Schedule 3.7 pending regulatory inquiries.

We recommend engaging Trident on the cap reduction and MAE carve-outs while holding firm on survival. If Trident will not withdraw the survival-period reduction for the core representations, the deal team should evaluate the walk-away posture in accordance with the client's stated mandate.

Prepared by: Structured Finance / Securitization Practice
Classification: Privileged & Confidential — Attorney Work Product
